Rolle und Protokollarchitektur des TCP/IP-Stacks

Das BSW-Modul TcpIp stellt in der AUTOSAR-Classic-Architektur die zentrale Vermittlungs- und Transportschicht für Ethernet-basierte On-Board- und Diagnosekommunikation bereit [SWS_TCPIP_00052], [SWS_TCPIP_00150]. Als Bindeglied zwischen der hardwarenahen Ethernet-Schnittstelle EthIf und den anfordernden oberen Softwareschichten – primär dem Socket-Adaptor (SoAd) sowie optionalen Complex Device Drivern (CDD) – kapselt das Modul internetbasierte Kommunikationsprotokolle standardisiert ab [SWS_TCPIP_00008], [SWS_TCPIP_00220], [SWS_TCPIP_00221]. Die Initialisierung erfolgt synchron über TcpIp_Init(), wobei der Stack-Startprozess nicht unbegrenzt blockieren darf [SWS_TCPIP_00002], während statische Versionsinformationen per TcpIp_GetVersionInfo() abgefragt werden können [SWS_TCPIP_00004], [SWS_TCPIP_00005].

Der Protokollstapel umfasst die Vermittlungsschicht für IPv4 gemäß RFC 791 samt Datagramm-Reassemblierung nach RFC 815 und Path MTU Discovery nach RFC 1191 [SWS_TCPIP_00053], [SWS_TCPIP_00054], [SWS_TCPIP_00055]. Im Dual-Stack-Betrieb unterstützt das Modul parallel IPv6 gemäß RFC 8200 mit Reassemblierung und Fragmentierung sowie Adressarchitektur-Vorgaben nach RFC 2464 und RFC 4291 [SWS_TCPIP_00153], [SWS_TCPIP_00160], [SWS_TCPIP_00161], [SWS_TCPIP_00232], [SWS_TCPIP_00269]. Zur Unterbindung von Angriffsmustern verbietet der Stack überlappende IPv6-Fragmente strikt gemäß RFC 5722 [SWS_TCPIP_00155]. Datagramme werden im Ethernet-Rahmen nach RFC 894 verpackt und an Netzmasken beziehungsweise Präfixe gebunden [SWS_TCPIP_00095], [SWS_TCPIP_00096].

Auf der Transportschicht stellt das Modul verbindungsloses UDP nach RFC 768 sowie verbindungsorientiertes TCP nach RFC 793 und RFC 1122 bereit [SWS_TCPIP_00060], [SWS_TCPIP_00061], [SWS_TCPIP_00103], [SWS_TCPIP_00104]. Für TCP sind Fluss- und Überlaststeuerungsmechanismen wie der Nagle-Algorithmus, Slow-Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit sowie Fast Recovery mit NewReno-Erweiterung verbindlich integriert [SWS_TCPIP_00062], [SWS_TCPIP_00063], [SWS_TCPIP_00064], [SWS_TCPIP_00168]. Ergänzt wird die Architektur durch Sicherheitsmechanismen: Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.2) nach RFC 5246 unter Ausschluss älterer Protokollversionen sowie IPsec/IKEv2 für authentifizierte Datagramme [SWS_TCPIP_00300], [SWS_TCPIP_00302], [SWS_TCPIP_00352], [SWS_TCPIP_00353].

Kontextdiagramm: Einbettung des TCP/IP-Stacks zwischen oberen Schichten, Hardwareabstraktion und Querschnittsmodulen. Quellen: [SWS_TCPIP_00008], [SWS_TCPIP_00027], [SWS_TCPIP_00028], [SWS_TCPIP_00220], [SWS_TCPIP_00361]

Zustandsverwaltung und Kommunikationssteuerung der Controller

Das Modul TcpIp führt für jeden über EthIf angebundenen Netzwerk-Controller eine eigenständige Zustandsmaschine und speichert die jeweils aktuell angeforderte Betriebsart [SWS_TCPIP_00083]. Die Steuerung erfolgt asynchron über die Service-Funktion TcpIp_RequestComMode(), wobei die Zustände TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE, TCPIP_STATE_ONHOLD und TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE aktiv angefordert werden können [SWS_TCPIP_00070], [SWS_TCPIP_00073]. Die internen Zustände TCPIP_STATE_STARTUP und TCPIP_STATE_SHUTDOWN dürfen durch Aufrufer nicht direkt übergeben werden und führen bei Entwicklungsfehlermeldung zur Rückweisung mit TCPIP_E_INV_ARG [SWS_TCPIP_00089]. Das zyklische Scheduling und die Überwachung von Zustandswechseln obliegen der Hauptfunktion TcpIp_MainFunction() [SWS_TCPIP_00026], [SWS_TCPIP_00136].

Wird für einen Controller im Zustand TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE der Zustand TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE angefordert, schaltet das Modul in TCPIP_STATE_STARTUP und aktiviert alle konfigurierten Adresszuweisungsmethoden und Zuweisungstrigger [SWS_TCPIP_00071], [SWS_TCPIP_00075]. Sobald mindestens eine IP-Adresse erfolgreich gebunden ist, wechselt der Controller autonom von TCPIP_STATE_STARTUP in TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE [SWS_TCPIP_00085]. Erst in diesem Online-Zustand akzeptiert der Stack neue TCP-Verbindungen und gestattet reguläre Datenübertragungen [SWS_TCPIP_00094].

Bei temporärem Verbindungsverlust (z. B. Link-Down) wechselt der Controller über TCPIP_STATE_ONHOLD in eine Wartestellung: Die Kommunikation wird deaktiviert und neue Sendeaufträge werden abgewiesen, bestehende Sockets und zugewiesene Adressen bleiben jedoch erhalten [SWS_TCPIP_00074], [SWS_TCPIP_00076]. Die oberen Schichten werden dabei per <Up>_LocalIpAddrAssignmentChg() mit dem Status TCPIP_IPADDR_STATE_ONHOLD informiert [SWS_TCPIP_00076], [SWS_TCPIP_00082]. Eine Rückkehr zu TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE reaktiviert den Stack und meldet TCPIP_IPADDR_STATE_ASSIGNED [SWS_TCPIP_00086]. Wird hingegen TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE angefordert oder werden alle Adressen freigegeben, schließt das Modul sämtliche Sockets des Controllers, gibt alle Ressourcen frei und meldet TCPIP_IPADDR_STATE_UNASSIGNED, bevor der Endzustand TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE über TCPIP_STATE_SHUTDOWN erreicht wird [SWS_TCPIP_00072], [SWS_TCPIP_00077], [SWS_TCPIP_00087], [SWS_TCPIP_00088].

Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklus und Transitionen eines EthIf-Controllers im TCP/IP-Stack. Quellen: [SWS_TCPIP_00070], [SWS_TCPIP_00073], [SWS_TCPIP_00075], [SWS_TCPIP_00076], [SWS_TCPIP_00077], [SWS_TCPIP_00085], [SWS_TCPIP_00086], [SWS_TCPIP_00087], [SWS_TCPIP_00088]

IP-Adresskonfiguration und dynamische Zuweisungsverfahren

Das Modul TcpIp verwaltet lokale Adressressourcen über eindeutige Indizes des Typs TcpIp_LocalAddrIdType [SWS_TCPIP_00030], [SWS_TCPIP_00099]. Über TcpIp_IpAddrAssignmentType werden vielfältige Konfigurationsmechanismen unterstützt: statische IP-Adressen (STATIC), Link-Local-Adressierung für DoIP oder allgemeine Netze (LINKLOCAL_DOIP, LINKLOCAL nach RFC 3927), DHCPv4/DHCPv6 (DHCP nach RFC 2131 und RFC 3315) sowie IPv6-Router-Advertisements (IPV6_ROUTER nach RFC 4862) [SWS_TCPIP_00057], [SWS_TCPIP_00058], [SWS_TCPIP_00065], [SWS_TCPIP_00157], [SWS_TCPIP_00166]. Sind mehrere Verfahren konfiguriert, besitzt die Zuweisung mit der höchsten Priorität Vorrang; wird eine höher priorisierte Adresse verfügbar, verdrängt sie bestehende Zuweisungen niedrigerer Priorität [SWS_TCPIP_00127].

Die Aktivierung manuell getriggerter Zuweisungen erfolgt über TcpIp_RequestIpAddrAssignment(), während die Freigabe über TcpIp_ReleaseIpAddrAssignment() eingeleitet wird [SWS_TCPIP_00037], [SWS_TCPIP_00078], [SWS_TCPIP_00116], [SWS_TCPIP_00117]. Ist eine Adresse auf automatischen Trigger (TCPIP_AUTOMATIC) konfiguriert, werden manuelle API-Aufrufe mit E_NOT_OK abgelehnt [SWS_TCPIP_00198], [SWS_TCPIP_00199]. Mit dem Typ TCPIP_IPADDR_ASSIGNMENT_ALL können alle konfigurierten manuellen Verfahren gleichzeitig angestoßen werden [SWS_TCPIP_00299]. Bei Multicast-Adresszuweisungen leitet das Modul die physische MAC-Adresse ab und trägt diese über EthIf_UpdatePhysAddrFilter() in den Hardwarefilter ein [SWS_TCPIP_00080], [SWS_TCPIP_00097], [SWS_TCPIP_00100].

Für Diagnose und Systemabfragen stellen TcpIp_GetIpAddr(), TcpIp_GetPhysAddr() und TcpIp_GetCtrlIdx() Funktionen zum synchronen Auslesen der aktuellen IP-Adresse, Netzmaske, Standard-Gateway, MAC-Adresse und Controller-Zuordnung bereit [SWS_TCPIP_00032], [SWS_TCPIP_00033], [SWS_TCPIP_00140], [SWS_TCPIP_00141]. Beim Einsatz von Non-Volatile Memory (TCPIP_STORE) liest der Stack beim Start persistierte Adressen aus dem NvM-Block oder speichert neu bezogene Adressen dort ab [SWS_TCPIP_00219]. Über TcpIp_ResetIpAssignment() können gelernte Adressen im NvM wieder auf ungültige Werte zurückgesetzt werden [SWS_TCPIP_00215], [SWS_TCPIP_00216], [SWS_TCPIP_00217]. Zur Integration in Server-Szenarien kann zudem ein integrierter DHCPv4-Server aktiviert werden, der IP-Adressen an Switch-Ports anhand empfangener MAC-Adressen zuweist [SWS_TCPIP_00200], [SWS_TCPIP_00201], [SWS_TCPIP_00218].

Aktivitätsdiagramm: Ablauf der Adresszuweisung und Prüfung auf Adresskonflikte (DAD). Quellen: [SWS_TCPIP_00075], [SWS_TCPIP_00116], [SWS_TCPIP_00159], [SWS_TCPIP_00219], [SWS_TCPIP_00282], [SWS_TCPIP_00283]

Socket-Lebenszyklus und Datentransport über UDP und TCP

Die Socket-Verwaltung basiert auf handles des Typs TcpIp_SocketIdType [SWS_TCPIP_00038]. Um Ressourcen strikt zu trennen, generiert das Modul für jeden konfigurierten Socket-Besitzer eine eigene Allokations-API TcpIp_<Up>GetSocket() (z. B. TcpIp_SoAdGetSocket()), wodurch Sockets exklusiv der anfordernden oberen Schicht zugeordnet werden [SWS_TCPIP_00018], [SWS_TCPIP_00222]. Beim Aufruf werden Domain (TCPIP_AF_INET oder TCPIP_AF_INET6) und Protokoll (TCPIP_IPPROTO_TCP oder TCPIP_IPPROTO_UDP) vorgegeben [SWS_TCPIP_00009], [SWS_TCPIP_00010]. Vor der Nutzung muss der Socket mittels TcpIp_Bind() an eine lokale Adresse und Portnummer gebunden werden [SWS_TCPIP_00015], [SWS_TCPIP_00111], [SWS_TCPIP_00130]. Dabei können Wildcards wie TCPIP_LOCALADDRID_ANY und TCPIP_PORT_ANY verwendet werden [SWS_TCPIP_00134], [SWS_TCPIP_00135]. Socket-Eigenschaften lassen sich dynamisch über TcpIp_ChangeParameter() anpassen, beispielsweise Nagle-Algorithmus, Keep-Alive, TCP-Empfangsfenstergröße oder Path-MTU-Ermittlung [SWS_TCPIP_00016], [SWS_TCPIP_00126], [SWS_TCPIP_00267].

Für UDP-Datenübertragungen dient der synchrone Dienst TcpIp_UdpTransmit() [SWS_TCPIP_00025], [SWS_TCPIP_00120]. Die Daten können entweder direkt als linearer Puffer übergeben oder bei Übergabe von NULL_PTR bedarfsgesteuert über die Callback-Funktion <Up>_CopyTxData() von der oberen Schicht abgeholt werden [SWS_TCPIP_00121], [SWS_TCPIP_00228]. Hardwareseitiges Checksummen-Offloading wird bei IPv4-, UDP- und TCP-Frames berücksichtigt, um Rechenzeit zu sparen [SWS_TCPIP_00203], [SWS_TCPIP_00204], [SWS_TCPIP_00280]. Bei EthIf_Transmit() setzt das Modul den Bestätigungsparameter stets auf FALSE [SWS_TCPIP_00131].

Sequenzdiagramm: UDP-Sendeablauf mit Cache-Prüfung und optionaler Pufferabholung. Quellen: [SWS_TCPIP_00025], [SWS_TCPIP_00120], [SWS_TCPIP_00121], [SWS_TCPIP_00191], [SWS_TCPIP_00228]

TCP-Verbindungen werden im Client-Modus über TcpIp_TcpConnect() initiiert, woraufhin der erfolgreiche Drei-Wege-Handshake der oberen Schicht über <Up>_TcpConnected() signalisiert wird [SWS_TCPIP_00022], [SWS_TCPIP_00112], [SWS_TCPIP_00227]. Im Server-Modus versetzt TcpIp_TcpListen() den Socket in den Abhörmodus; neu eingehende Verbindungen meldet der Stack über <Up>_TcpAccepted() unter Vergabe eines neuen Verbindungssockets [SWS_TCPIP_00023], [SWS_TCPIP_00113], [SWS_TCPIP_00226]. Das Senden erfolgt asynchron mittels TcpIp_TcpTransmit(), wobei ForceRetrieve erzwingen kann, dass Daten sofort vollständig via <Up>_CopyTxData() kopiert werden [SWS_TCPIP_00050], [SWS_TCPIP_00123], [SWS_TCPIP_00124], [SWS_TCPIP_00125]. Positiv quittierte TCP-Segmente meldet der Stack per <Up>_TxConfirmation() [SWS_TCPIP_00225].

Eingehende Daten werden von EthIf über TcpIp_RxIndication() entgegengenommen [SWS_TCPIP_00029]. Der Stack prüft lokale Adresstabellen und mappt Datagramme anhand Ziel-IP und Port auf aktive Sockets [SWS_TCPIP_00169], [SWS_TCPIP_00170], [SWS_TCPIP_00172], [SWS_TCPIP_00173]. Eingehende TCP-Broadcast- oder Multicast-Pakete werden verworfen [SWS_TCPIP_00174]. Nutzdaten werden über <Up>_RxIndication() an die Anwendung übergeben [SWS_TCPIP_00223]. Die Anwendung bestätigt den Verzehr von TCP-Daten mittels TcpIp_TcpReceived(), was dem Stack die Freigabe und Vergrößerung des TCP-Empfangsfensters ermöglicht [SWS_TCPIP_00024], [SWS_TCPIP_00115]. Beendet wird ein Socket über TcpIp_Close(), wahlweise geordnet per FIN-Handshake (Abort=FALSE) oder abrupt per RST-Segment (Abort=TRUE) [SWS_TCPIP_00017], [SWS_TCPIP_00109], [SWS_TCPIP_00110]. Zustandsänderungen wie Verbindungsabbruch oder Schließen teilt der Stack über <Up>_TcpIpEvent() mit [SWS_TCPIP_00031], [SWS_TCPIP_00144].

Sequenzdiagramm: TCP-Verbindungsaufbau, Nutzdatenübertragung und Empfangsfensterverwaltung. Quellen: [SWS_TCPIP_00022], [SWS_TCPIP_00024], [SWS_TCPIP_00050], [SWS_TCPIP_00115], [SWS_TCPIP_00125], [SWS_TCPIP_00225], [SWS_TCPIP_00227]

Sicherheitsfunktionen, Adressauflösung und Diagnosemetriken

Zur Auflösung von IP-Adressen in physikalische MAC-Adressen implementiert TcpIp das Address Resolution Protocol (ARP nach RFC 826) für IPv4 und Neighbor Discovery (NDP nach RFC 4861) für IPv6 [SWS_TCPIP_00056], [SWS_TCPIP_00164]. Die Cache-Größen sind über Parameter wie TcpIpArpTableSizeMax und TcpIpNdpMaxNeighborCacheSize limitiert; bei vollem Cache verdrängen neue Einträge die ältesten (LRU) [SWS_TCPIP_00090], [SWS_TCPIP_00263], [SWS_TCPIP_00264]. Ungenutzte Einträge altern nach Ablauf von TcpIpArpTableEntryTimeout aus [SWS_TCPIP_00091]. Zur Härtung gegen Spoofing kann über TcpIpNdpDefensiveProcessing eine defensive NDP-Verarbeitung aktiviert werden, die unaufgeforderte Neighbor Advertisements verwirft und Cache-Updates bei Neighbor Solicitations unterbindet [SWS_TCPIP_00261], [SWS_TCPIP_00262]. Flooding-Schutzmechanismen begrenzen ARP-Wiederholungen zeitlich [SWS_TCPIP_00350]. Tabelleninhalte können von der Anwendung über TcpIp_GetArpCacheEntries() und TcpIp_GetNdpCacheEntries() ausgelesen werden [SWS_TCPIP_00271], [SWS_TCPIP_00275], [SWS_TCPIP_91001], [SWS_TCPIP_91002], [SWS_TCPIP_91003], [SWS_TCPIP_91004].

Fehlt beim Senden die Ziel-MAC-Adresse im Cache, steuert TcpIpArpPacketQueueEnabled beziehungsweise TcpIpNdpPacketQueueEnabled das Verhalten: Ist das Queueing aktiv, wird die Adressauflösung initiiert, das Paket zwischengespeichert und der Sendeauftrag mit E_OK quittiert; andernfalls wird die Anfrage mit E_NOT_OK abgelehnt [SWS_TCPIP_00191], [SWS_TCPIP_00192], [SWS_TCPIP_00193]. Statusänderungen im Cache teilt das Modul über <Up_PhysAddrTableChg>() mit [SWS_TCPIP_00142], [SWS_TCPIP_00143].

Für sichere Verbindungen stellt der Stack TLS 1.2 mit PSK-Unterstützung (Pre-Shared Keys) bereit [SWS_TCPIP_00300], [SWS_TCPIP_91011]. Die Aushandlung stützt sich auf Callbacks wie <Up_TlsGetCurrentTime>(), <Up_TlsServerGetPskIdentityHint>() sowie Client- und Server-PSK-Abfragen ab, die Schlüssel über das Crypto Service Manager Modul (Csm) referenzieren [SWS_TCPIP_00028], [SWS_TCPIP_91012], [SWS_TCPIP_91013], [SWS_TCPIP_91014], [SWS_TCPIP_91015]. Auf IP-Ebene schützt IPsec den Datenstrom gemäß Security Policy Database (SPD): Datagramme werden priorisiert geprüft und gemäß Policy verarbeitet (TCPIP_IPSEC_POLICY_PROTECT, TCPIP_IPSEC_POLICY_BYPASS, TCPIP_IPSEC_POLICY_DISCARD) [SWS_TCPIP_00357], [SWS_TCPIP_00359], [SWS_TCPIP_00360]. Sicherheitsrelevante Vorfälle werden an den Intrusion Detection System Manager (IdsM) gemeldet [SWS_TCPIP_00361]. ICMP-Nachrichten (ICMPv4/ICMPv6) können über TcpIp_IcmpTransmit() und TcpIp_IcmpV6Transmit() abgesetzt oder bei Bedarf an <Up_IcmpMsgHandler>() durchgereicht werden [SWS_TCPIP_00039], [SWS_TCPIP_00118], [SWS_TCPIP_00187], [SWS_TCPIP_00230], [SWS_TCPIP_00270], [SWS_TCPIP_00297].

Zur Netzwerküberwachung und Performance-Analyse erfasst das Modul Zähler für verworfene Pakete, die über TcpIp_GetAndResetMeasurementData() abgefragt und zurückgesetzt werden können [SWS_TCPIP_00284], [SWS_TCPIP_00286], [SWS_TCPIP_91006]. Gemäß TcpIp_MeasurementIdxType werden Verwürfe wegen ungültiger TCP- oder UDP-Ports (TCPIP_MEAS_DROP_TCP, TCPIP_MEAS_DROP_UDP) sowie ungültiger IPv4- oder IPv6-Zieladressen (TCPIP_MEAS_DROP_IPV4, TCPIP_MEAS_DROP_IPV6) erfasst, wobei Zählerüberläufe ausgeschlossen sind [SWS_TCPIP_00287], [SWS_TCPIP_00288], [SWS_TCPIP_00289], [SWS_TCPIP_00290], [SWS_TCPIP_00294], [SWS_TCPIP_00296], [SWS_TCPIP_91010].

Verhalten im Fehlerfall

Das Modul TcpIp unterscheidet streng zwischen Entwicklungsfehlern (Development Errors) und Laufzeitfehlern (Runtime Errors), die über den Default Error Tracer (Det) gemeldet werden [SWS_TCPIP_00027], [SWS_TCPIP_00042], [SWS_TCPIP_00255]. Wird eine Stack-API vor dem erfolgreichen Abschluss von TcpIp_Init() aufgerufen, wird der Fehler TCPIP_E_UNINIT gemeldet und die Ausführung abgewiesen [SWS_TCPIP_00042], [SWS_TCPIP_00285]. Unzulässige Nullzeiger führen zu TCPIP_E_PARAM_POINTER [SWS_TCPIP_00042]. Ungültige Funktionsargumente – wie unzulässige Controller-Zustände, widersprüchliche Domain-Typen bei TcpIp_GetIpAddr() oder fehlerhafte Längen bei DHCP-Optionen – lösen TCPIP_E_INV_ARG aus [SWS_TCPIP_00089], [SWS_TCPIP_00205], [SWS_TCPIP_00206], [SWS_TCPIP_00233], [SWS_TCPIP_00235], [SWS_TCPIP_00245]. Nicht unterstützte Protokollfamilien in TcpIp_<Up>GetSocket() melden TCPIP_E_AFNOSUPPORT [SWS_TCPIP_00128].

Kollisionen bei der Socket-Bindung werden frühzeitig abgefangen: Ist ein lokaler Port auf demselben Interface bereits belegt, schlägt TcpIp_Bind() fehl und meldet bei aktivem DET den Fehler TCPIP_E_ADDRINUSE [SWS_TCPIP_00042], [SWS_TCPIP_00146]. Ist die übergebene LocalAddrId ungültig oder noch nicht zugewiesen, verweigert die Bindung mit E_NOT_OK beziehungsweise TCPIP_E_ADDRNOTAVAIL [SWS_TCPIP_00147], [SWS_TCPIP_00254].

Netzwerk- und Protokollfehler zur Laufzeit werden über Det_ReportRuntimeError() signalisiert [SWS_TCPIP_00255]. Der Fehler TCPIP_E_TIMEDOUT tritt auf, wenn ein SYN-Verbindungsversuch unbeantwortet bleibt, ein TCP-Keep-Alive-Timer abläuft oder die maximale Anzahl von TCP-Retransmissions überschritten wird [SWS_TCPIP_00202], [SWS_TCPIP_00256]. Empfängt der Stack ICMP-Meldungen des Typs Destination Unreachable, differenziert er entsprechend: TCPIP_E_CONNREFUSED bei Port- oder Protokoll-Unerreichbarkeit [SWS_TCPIP_00257], TCPIP_E_HOSTUNREACH bei fehlender Route zum Zielhost [SWS_TCPIP_00258] sowie TCPIP_E_PACKETTOBIG bei gesetztem Don't-Fragment-Bit (DF) und unzureichender MTU [SWS_TCPIP_00259]. Ein Adresskonflikt bei der Duplicate Address Detection (DAD) für IPv4 oder IPv6 meldet TCPIP_E_DADCONFLICT und ruft den konfigurierten Callout <Up_DADAddressConflict>() auf, um Gegenmaßnahmen einzuleiten [SWS_TCPIP_00282], [SWS_TCPIP_00283], [SWS_TCPIP_91005].

Weiterführende Detailbelege

Die Spezifikation von TcpIp stützt sich auf normative Anforderungen ab, die Kernfunktionen, Datenstrukturen und Schnittstellen eindeutig regeln. Die nachfolgende Tabelle ordnet die zentralen Spezifikationsanker thematisch ein:

Bereich Wesentliche Requirements Inhaltliche Kurzbeschreibung
Initialisierung und Versionierung [SWS_TCPIP_00002], [SWS_TCPIP_00004], [SWS_TCPIP_00067] Nicht-blockierender Stackstart, Bereitstellung statischer Versionsangaben und Konfigurationsstruktur.
Controller-Zustandsmaschine [SWS_TCPIP_00070], [SWS_TCPIP_00073], [SWS_TCPIP_00083] Zustandsverwaltung je EthIf-Controller mit OFFLINE, STARTUP, ONLINE, ONHOLD und SHUTDOWN.
IP-Adressierung und Zuweisung [SWS_TCPIP_00037], [SWS_TCPIP_00065], [SWS_TCPIP_00127] Priorisierte Zuweisungsverfahren (Static, DHCPv4/v6, Link-Local, Router Advertisement, NvM-Persistenz).
Socket-Verwaltung und API [SWS_TCPIP_00015], [SWS_TCPIP_00018], [SWS_TCPIP_00222] Exklusive Socket-Allokation für Upper Layers, Bindung an lokale Adressen/Ports und Wildcards.
Datentransport (UDP / TCP) [SWS_TCPIP_00025], [SWS_TCPIP_00050], [SWS_TCPIP_00124] Synchrone/asynchrone Sendeoperationen, Pufferabruf via CopyTxData und Empfangsfensterfortschreibung.
Sicherheit (TLS / IPsec / NDP) [SWS_TCPIP_00261], [SWS_TCPIP_00300], [SWS_TCPIP_00359] Defensives NDP gegen Spoofing, TLS 1.2 PSK Handshake und Security Policy Database für IPsec.
Fehlerbehandlung und Metriken [SWS_TCPIP_00042], [SWS_TCPIP_00255], [SWS_TCPIP_91006] DET-Entwicklungsfehler, Laufzeitfehler bei Verbindungsabbrüchen/Timeouts und Erfassung von Drop-Zählern.

Dieser Modul-Leitfaden wurde automatisiert auf Basis der AUTOSAR-Spezifikation R20-11 für das Classic-Modul tcpip erstellt.

TCP/IP Stack (TcpIp)

Provides IPv4/IPv6 networking, TCP/UDP sockets, ARP, ICMP, and DHCP services.

Funktionen — Übersicht

  • void TcpIp_Init (const TcpIp_ConfigType* ConfigPtr); This service initializes the TCP/ IP Stack.
  • void TcpIp_GetVersionInfo (Std_VersionInfoType* versioninfo); Returns the version information.

Typen — Übersicht

  • struct TcpIp_ConfigType Configuration data structure of the Tcp Ip module.
  • TcpIp_DomainType Tcp Ip address families.
  • TcpIp_ProtocolType Protocol type used by a socket.
  • struct TcpIp_SockAddrType Generic structure used by APIs to specify an IP address.
  • struct TcpIp_SockAddrInetType This structure defines an IPv4 address type which can be derived from the generic address structure via cast.
  • struct TcpIp_SockAddrInet6Type This structure defines a IPv6 address type which can be derived from the generic address structure via cast.
  • TcpIp_LocalAddrIdType Address identification type for unique identification of a local IP address and Eth If Controller configured in the Tcp Ip module.
  • TcpIp_SocketIdType Socket identifier type for unique identification of a Tcp Ip stack socket.
  • enum TcpIp_StateType Specifies the Tcp Ip state for a specific Eth If controller.
  • enum TcpIp_IpAddrStateType Specifies the state of local IP a ddress assignment
  • TcpIp_EventType Events reported by Tcp Ip.
  • TcpIp_IpAddrAssignmentType IPv6 address assignment policy.
  • enum TcpIp_ReturnType Tcp Ip specific return type.
  • TcpIp_ParamIdType Type TcpIp_ParamIdType.
  • TcpIpIpAddrWildcardType IP address wildcard.
  • TcpIpIp6AddrWildcardType IP6 address wildcard.
  • TcpIpPortWildcardType Port wildcard.
  • TcpIpLocalAddrIdWildcardType Local Addr Id wildcard.
  • TcpIp_ArpCacheEntryType Tcp Ip_ Arp Cache Entries elements type
  • TcpIp_NdpCacheEntryType Tcp Ip_ Ndp Cache Entries elements type
  • TcpIp_MeasurementIdxType Index to select specific measurement data
  • TcpIp_TlsConnectionIdType TLS connection identifier type for unique identification of a TLS connection.

void TcpIp_Init (const TcpIp_ConfigType* ConfigPtr);

This service initializes the TCP/ IP Stack. Tcp Ip_ Init may not block the start - up process for an indefinite amount of time. Caveats: The call of this service is mandatory before using the Tcp Ip instance for further processing.

function [SWS_TCPIP_00225] 📄 PDF

void <<<<>>>> (TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketId, uint16 Length);

The TCP/ IP stack calls this function after the data has been acknowledged by the peer for TCP. Caveats: The upper layer might not be able to determine exactly which data bytes have been confirmed.

function [SWS_TCPIP_00226] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType <<<<>>>> (TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketId, TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketId Connected, const TcpIp_SockAddrType* Remote AddrPtr);

This service gets called if the stack put a socket into the listen mode before (as server) and a peer connected to it (as client). In detail: T he TCP/ IP stack calls this function after a socket was set into the listen state with Tcp Ip_ Tcp Listen() and a TCP connection is requested by the peer.

function [SWS_TCPIP_00227] 📄 PDF

void <<<<>>>> (TcpIp_SocketIdType SocketId);

This service gets called if the stack initiated a TCP connection before (as client) and the peer (the server) acknowledged the connection set up. In detail: The TCP/ IP stack calls this function after a socket was requested to connect with Tcp Ip_ Tcp Conn ect() and a TCP connection is confirmed by the peer. The parameter value of Socket Id equals the Socket Id value of the preceeding Tcp Ip_ Tcp Connect() call.

=== SYSTEM PROMPT ===
Du bist der KI-Kurations-Assistent des Dokumentationssystems autodocs (AUTOSAR).
Verfasse den Modul-Leitfaden (<div class="ai module-guide">) für das classic-Modul 'tcpip' im Release R20-11.

RICHTLINIEN (bindend):
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei wird von den Prompt-Rezepten (`_src/tools/prompt_recipes.py`)
wörtlich in jeden Prompt eingebettet. Jede Änderung ändert daher alle
Prompt-Hashes; bestehende KI-Texte gelten dann als veraltet und werden neu
erzeugt. Herkunft und Ablage der Ausgaben regelt `_src/lib_ai_store.py`.

## Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch. Die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter Schritt
  und nie Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und Kennungen wie `[SWS_…]` bleiben
  unverändert.

## Struktur

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai usage` für
  Verwendungshinweise an einem Spezifikationselement, `ai module-guide` für
  Modul-Leitfäden) und endet mit genau einem `<p class="ai-note">` (KI-Hinweis).
- Erlaubte Elemente im Fragment: `div`, `p`, `h4`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `code`,
  `strong`, `em`, `a`, `span`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`.
  Keine Skripte, keine Stile, keine Bilder, kein `<svg>` (Diagramme siehe unten).
- Alle Tags korrekt geschlossen und verschachtelt.

## Belegpflicht

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist zu belegen. Belege stammen ausschließlich aus dem
  Payload des Prompts; nichts darf aus anderem Wissen als Beleg ausgegeben werden.
- Verweis auf ein Spezifikationselement oder Requirement (nur IDs, die im
  Payload vorkommen):
  `<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_…">[SWS_…]</a>` — ohne `href`; den
  Link setzt der Generator.
- Verweis auf eine Dokumentstelle (nur Dokument/Seite aus dem Payload):
  `<span class="docref" data-doc="<Dokument-ID>" data-page="<Seite>">Kurzname §x.y „Titel“</span>`.
- Niemals URLs ausgeben, insbesondere keine PDF-URLs.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Quellen schweigen, sind höchstens 3 Annahmen je Text und 2 je
  Diagramm erlaubt.
- Jede Annahme ist im Text als Interpretation erkennbar („dürfte“, „vermutlich“,
  „Interpretation:“) und wird am Ende des Fragments in einem Kommentar
  `<!-- annahmen: 1) … – Begründung: … -->` aufgezählt.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekulieren.

## Diagramme

Ein Diagramm nur, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet:

- Sequenzdiagramm: Abläufe ab 3 Schritten oder mit nicht offensichtlicher
  Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramm: ab 3 beteiligten Komponenten.
- Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Aktivitätsdiagramm: Entscheidungs- oder Verarbeitungsabläufe mit Verzweigung.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert. Jedes Diagramm steht im
Fragment als Platzhalter `<div class="diagram" id="diag-<kurzname>"></div>`,
direkt gefolgt von `<p class="diagram-note"><Diagrammart>: <Kernaussage>.
Quellen: <Belege></p>`. Die Diagrammquelle wird separat ausgegeben (Format
legt der Prompt fest).

LEITBILD (Umfang und Aufbau orientieren sich an den bewährten Adaptive-Modulleitfäden):
- 900–1600 Wörter in 5–8 thematischen Abschnitten mit <h4>-Überschriften, die das
  Modul erschließen (z. B. Rolle und Systemgrenze, zentrale Abläufe vom Start bis zur
  Nutzung, Daten- und Interaktionsformen, Betriebsregeln und Randbedingungen,
  Konfiguration/Instanzbezug, Verhalten im Fehlerfall). Die Überschriften sind
  modulspezifisch zu formulieren, nicht generisch.
- Ein Abschnitt „Verhalten im Fehlerfall“ und am Ende ein Abschnitt
  „Weiterführende Detailbelege“ (die wichtigsten Requirements/Dokumentstellen kurz
  eingeordnet).
- Jeder Absatz enthält mindestens einen Beleg (Requirement-ID oder Dokumentstelle).
- 4–10 Diagramme, wo sie Mehrwert bieten: Sequenzdiagramme für zentrale Abläufe,
  Zustandsdiagramme für Lebenszyklen, Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramme für die
  Einbettung, Aktivitätsdiagramme für Entscheidungen. Die Schaubilder der Spezifikation
  (Payload-Einträge mit "figure": true) sind Ausgangspunkt: übernimm ihre Aussage,
  wo sie den Text stützen, und verbessere ihre Lesbarkeit.
- Das Fragment beginnt mit <div class="ai module-guide"> und endet mit
  <p class="ai-note">…</p></div>.

AUSGABEFORMAT (verbindlich, nichts außerhalb dieser Blöcke):
<<<FRAGMENT
<div class="…"> … </div>
FRAGMENT>>>
Danach je Diagramm-Platzhalter genau ein Block:
<<<DIAGRAM diag-<kurzname> seq
<JSON nach dem Sequenz-Schema>
DIAGRAM>>>
oder
<<<DIAGRAM diag-<kurzname> dot
<Graphviz-digraph ohne Stilattribute (Farben/Schriften setzt der Generator)>
DIAGRAM>>>

Sequenz-Schema (JSON):
{"titel": str, "teilnehmer": [{"name": str}], "schritte": [
  {"art": "nachricht", "von": <idx>, "nach": <idx>, "text": [str], "pfeil": "voll"|"offen", "gestrichelt": bool},
  {"art": "selbst", "teilnehmer": <idx>, "text": [str]},
  {"art": "notiz", "ueber": [<idx>, <idx>], "text": [str]},
  {"art": "abschnitt", "text": str},
  {"art": "rahmen", "typ": "alt"|"opt"|"loop", "guard": str}, {"art": "trenner", "guard": str}, {"art": "rahmen-ende"}
]}
Antworten/Rückgaben: "pfeil": "offen", "gestrichelt": true. Zustands-, Kontext- und Aktivitätsdiagramme als dot.

  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00052",
   "text": "The TCP/IP stack shal l consist of sub modules implementing specific fu nctionalities defined in the s ubchapters below."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00053",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall implement the Internet Protocol as defined in IETF RFC 791 ( Internet Protocol of version 4 )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00054",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall be able to reassemb le incoming datagrams that are fragmented according to IETF RFC 815 ( IP Datagram Reassembly Algorithms )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00055",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall discover the maximum transmission unit (MTU) for a path as d efined in IETF RFC 1191 ( Path MTU Discovery )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00056",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall implement the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) as defined in IETF RFC 826."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00057",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the dynamic configuration of IPv4 Link Local addresses as defined in IETF RFC 3927 ( Dynamic Configuration of IPv4 Link - Local Addresses )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00058",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall implement the client and the serve r part of the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCPv4) for the dynamic configuration of IPv4 addresses as defined in IETF RFC 2131 (Dynami c Host Configuration Protocol)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00059",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the transmission and reception of I nternet Control Message Protocol (ICMP v4 ) messages as defined in IETF RFC 792 ( Internet Control Message Protocol in version 4 )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00060",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall implement the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) as defined in IETF RFC 768 ( User Datagram Protocol )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00061",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall implement the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) as defined in IETF RFC 793 ( Transmission Control Protocol )"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00062",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the Window and Acknowledgment Strategies in TCP as defined in ETF RFC 1122:  4.2.3.1 Retransmission Timeout Calculation  4.2.3.2 When to Send an ACK Segment  4.2.3.3 When to Send a Window Update Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 31 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp  4.2.3.4 When to Send Data ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00063",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall implement the Nagle Algorithm as defined in IETF RFC 1122: 4.2.3.4 When to Send Data ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00064",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall implement the congestion control strategies slow - start, congestion a voidance , fast retransmit and fast recovery as defined in IETF RFC 5681."
  },
  {

  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00071",
   "text": "If TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE is request ed , the TcpIp module shall initiate activation of the TcpIp communication on the related EthIf controller (e.g. start IP - Address assignment according to the con figured IP address assignment policy for the EthIf controller )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00072",
   "text": "If TCPIP_ STATE_OFFLINE is requested , the TcpIp module shall initiate deactivation of the TcpIp communication on the related EthIf controller (e.g. close all sockets using the specified EthIf controller)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00073",
   "text": "Name Tcp Ip_ State Type Kind Enumeration Range TCPIP_ STATE_ ONLINE -- TCP/ IP stack state for a specific Eth If controller is ONLINE, i.e. communication via at least one IP address is possible. TCPIP_ STATE_ ONHOLD -- TCP/ IP stack state for a specific Eth If controller is ONHOLD, i.e. no communication is currently possibl e (e.g. link down). TCPIP_ STATE_ OFFLINE -- TCP/ IP stack state for a specific Eth If controller is OFFLINE, i.e. no communication is possible. TCPIP_ STATE_ -- TCP/ IP stack state for a specific Eth If controller is STARTUP, Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00074",
   "text": "If TCPIP_STATE_ONHOLD is requested, th e TcpIp module shall set the TcpIp communication to on hold, i.e. new transmit requests shall not be accepted, but sockets and assigned IP addresses shall be kept."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00075",
   "text": "I f TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE is requested for a n EthIf controller and the current state is TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE for that EthIf controller , the TcpIp module shall Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 48 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp (a) enable all IP address assignments according to the configured assignment methods ( TcpIpAssignmentMethod ) and triggers ( TcpIpAssignmentTrigger ) for that EthIf controller. (Note: I f the assignment trigger is configured to TCPIP_MANUAL no assignment is actually performed but initiation by the upper layer enabled) and (b) enter the state…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00076",
   "text": "If TCPIP_STATE_ONHOLD is requested for an EthIf controller and the current state is TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE for that EthIf controller , the TcpIp module shall (a) notify the upper layer via Up _L ocalIpAddrAssignmentChg() with State TCPIP_IPADDR_STATE_ONHOLD for all assigned IP addresses of the related EthIf controller, and (b) deactivate the communication within the TcpIp module for the related EthIf controller, and (c) enter the state TCPIP_STATE_ONHOLD for the EthIf controller ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00077",
   "text": "If TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE is requested or all assigned IP address have been released for an EthIf controller and the current state is TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE or TCPIP_STATE_O NHOLD for that EthIf controller , the TcpIp module shall (a) call Up _LocalIpAddrAssignmentChg() with State TCPIP_IPADD R_STATE_UNASSIGNED for all assigned IP addresses of the related EthIf controller, (b) deactivate the communication within the TcpIp module for the related EthIf controller, (c) release related resources, i.e. any socket using the EthIf controller shall be closed and thereafter any IP address assigned to the Eth…"
  },

Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value Std _ Return - Type E_ OK: The request has been accepted E_ NOT_ OK: The request has not been accepted Description By this API service the local IP address assignment for the IP address specified by L…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00079",
   "text": "In case TcpIp_RequestIpAddrAssignment() is called with parameter Type set to TCPIP_IPADDR_ASSIGNMENT_STATIC and no TcpIpStaticIpAddressConfig container is con figured for the LocalAddr specified by parameter LocalAddrId, TcpIp shall assign the IP address, netmask and default router specified by parameter LocalIpAddrPtr, Netmask and DefaultRouterPtr as soon as TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE is requested or immediately if alr eady requested."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00080",
   "text": "I n case a multicast address is assigned, TcpIp shall derive the related physical address from the multicast IP address and add the derived address to the Eth MAC address filter by ca lling EthIf_ UpdatePhys - AddrFilter () with action se t to ETH_ ADD_TO_FILTER ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00082",
   "text": "Name Tcp Ip_ Ip Addr State Type Kind Enumeration Range TCPIP_ IPADDR_ STATE_ ASSIGNED -- local IP address is assigned TCPIP_ IPADDR_ STATE_ ONHOLD -- local IP address is assigned, but cannot be used as the network is not active TCPIP_ IPADDR_ STATE_ UNASSIGNED -- local IP address is unassigned Description Specifies the state of local IP a ddress assignment Available via Tcp Ip.h"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00083",
   "text": "The TcpIp module shall maintain a separate state for each EthIf controller used by the TcpIp module , store the latest state request and distinguish at least the following states: TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE, TCPI P_STATE_STARTUP, TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE, TCPIP_STATE_ONHOLD, and TCPIP_STATE_SHUTDOWN."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00085",
   "text": "If at least one IP address has been successfully assigned to an EthIf controller and the current state is TCPIP_STATE_ STARTU P for that EthIf controller, the TcpIp module shall enter the state TCPIP_STATE_ ONLINE for the EthIf controller ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00086",
   "text": "If TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE is requested for an EthIf controller and the current state is TCPIP_STATE_ONHOLD for that EthIf controller, the TcpIp module shall (a) reactivate the communication within the TcpIp module for the related EthIf cont roller, (b) call Up _LocalIpAddrAssignmentChg() with State TCPIP_IPADDR_STATE_ ASSIGNED for all assigned IP addresses of the related EthIf controller, and Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 49 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp (c) enter the state TCPIP_STATE_ON LINE for the EthIf controller ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00087",
   "text": "If the current state of an EthIf controller is TCPIP_STATE_SHUTDOWN and all related resources have been released, the TcpIp module shall enter the state TCPIP_STATE_O FFLINE for the EthIf controller ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00088",
   "text": "I f TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE is requested for an EthIf controller and the current state is TCPIP_STATE_STARTUP for that EthIf controller , the TcpIp module shall (a) abort all ongoing IP address assignment actions appropriate and (b) enter the state TCPIP_STATE_ OFFLINE for the EthIf controller ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00089",
   "text": "If TCPIP_STATE_STARTUP or TCPIP_STATE_SHUTDOW N is requested as state the function TcpIp_RequestComMode shall abort with E_NOT_OK and report TCPIP_E_INV_ARG if development error detection is enabled."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00090",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall limit the number of ARP table (address resolution cache) entries to the number specified by the configuration parameter TcpIpArpTableSizeMax ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00091",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall remove entries of the ARP table if they are not used for the timeout specified by the configuratio n parameter TcpIpArpTableEntryTimeout. If TcpIpArpTableEntryTimeout is set to INF , the TcpIp module shall never remove entries from the ARP table."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00092",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall use the information from each received IP packet to update the ARP tab le in addition to received ARP packets."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00093",
   "text": "On assignment of a new IP address the TcpIp shall send a co nfigurable number ( TcpIpArpNumGratuitousARPonStartup ) of gratuitous ARP replies according to IETF RFC 2002, section 4.6, second indent. These announcements shall be timed according to IETF RFC 5227 section 2.3. Announcing an Address."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00094",
   "text": "The TcpIp modu le shall only accept new TCP connections if the related EthIf controller is in state TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00095",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall encapsulate IP packets in Ethernet frames according to IETF RFC 894."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00096",
   "text": "The TcpIp shal l support the identification of the network an IP address belongs to, by using a network mask (prefix) in addition to the IP address according to IETF RFC 4632, section 3.1."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00097",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall be able to transmit IP datagrams to a group of hosts identified by a single IP destination address (multicast address) according to IETF RFC 1112, section 4, 6.2, and 6.4."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00098",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall be able to receive multicast IP datagrams identified by a single IP destination address (multicast address) acc ording to IETF RFC 1112, section 4 and 7.2 (excluding the requirement for IGMP ) ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00099",
   "text": "The TcpIp sha ll maintain a table of local IP addresses, which can be assigned to an EthIf controller during runtime according to the configuration container TcpIpLocalAddr (including its subcontainers)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00100",
   "text": "In case no TcpIpStaticAddressConfig is provided, the TcpIp shall enable to specify a multicast IP address during runtime via TcpIp_RequestIpAddrAssignment()."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00101",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall choose the correct next hop for each datagram it sends according to IETF RFC 1122, section 3.3.1.1. (IPv4) and IETF RFC4861 section 5.2. Conceptual Sending Algorithm (IPv6)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00102",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall fulfill the Internet Protocol related requi rements specified by IETF RFC 1122, section 3.2.1.1 (Version number), 3.2.1.2 (Checksum), 3.2.1.3 (Addressing), 3.2.1.7 (TTL), and 3.3.2 (Reassembly)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00103",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall fulfill the UDP related requirements sp ecified by IETF RFC 1122, section 4.1.3.1 (Ports), 4.1.3.4 (UDP Checksums), and 4.1.3.6 (Invalid Addresses)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00104",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall fulfill the TCP related requirements specified by IETF RFC 1122, section 4.2.2.3 (Window Size), 4.2.2.5 (TCP Options), 4.2.2.6 (MSS), 4.2.2.7 (Checksum), 4.2.2.9 (Initial sequence number selection), 4.2.2.10 (Simultaneous Open Attempts), 4.2.2.11 (Recovery from Old Duplicate SYN), 4.2.2.13 (Closing a Connection, excluding “half - duplex close”) , 4.2.2.15 (Retransmission Timeout), 4.2.2.16 (Managing the Window ), 4.2.2.17 (Probing Zero Windows), 4.2.2.18 (Passive OPEN Calls), 4.2.2.19 (TTL), 4.2.3.2 (delayed ACK), 4.2.3.6 (TCP Keep Alive), and 4.2.3.10 (Remote Address Validati…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00109",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_Close() shall perform the following actions for the socket specified by SocketId in case it is a TCP socket: (a) if the connection is active and (a1) abort = FALSE: the connection shall be terminated after performing a regular connection t ermination handshake and releasing all related resources. (a2) abort = TRUE: connection shall immediately be terminated by sending a RST - Segment and releasing all related resources. Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 66 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp (b) if the socket is in the Listen state, the Listen state s…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00110",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_Close() shall release all related resources immediately for the socket specified by SocketId in case it is a UDP socket ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00111",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_ Bind() shall bind the socket specified by parameter SocketId to the local resource specified by parameters LocalAddrId and PortPtr."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00112",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_TcpConnect() shall establish a TCP conn ection between the local socket specified by parameter SocketId and the remote socket specified with parameter RemoteAddrPtr."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00113",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_TcpListen() shall put the socket specified by SocketId to the listen state (i.e. local socket is listening for incoming connections)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00115",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_TcpReceived() shall increase the TCP receive window of the socket specified by Sock etId considering the number of finally consumed bytes specified by Length."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00116",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_ RequestIpAddrAssignment () shall initiate the local IP address assignment according to the IP addre ss table entry specified by LocalAddId using the method specified by Type."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00117",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_ Re lease pAddrAssignment () shall release the local IP address assignment related to the IP address table entry specified by LocalAddId."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00118",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_ IcmpTransmit () shall (a) construct an ICMP message according to the parameters Type, Code, DataLength and DataPtr and (b) transmit the ICMP message using the local IP address and EthIf controller specified by LocalIpAddrId to the destination specified by RemoteAddrPtr using a time to live value according to the parameter Ttl."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00120",
   "text": "With respect to SWS_TCPIP_00191 and SWS_TCPIP_00193, the service TcpIp_UdpTransmit() shall immediately transmit TotalLength data bytes via UDP and the socket specified by SocketId to a remote socket specified by R emoteAddrPtr according to the sequence diagram specified in section 9.5 ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00121",
   "text": "DataPtr shall either point to a linear buffer of TotalLength bytes containing the data for transmission or be a NULL_PTR. For data transmission the service TcpI p_UdpTransmit() shal l either use all data from the linear buffer if Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 92 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp DataPtr is not a NULL_PTR , or retrieve TotalLength data bytes from the upper layer by calling Up _CopyTxData() one or multiple times in the context of this service otherwise ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00123",
   "text": "The service TcpIp _Tcp Transmit() shall tra nsmit data via TCP and the socket specified by SocketId to the connected remote socket according to the sequence diagram specified in section 9.4 ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00124",
   "text": "DataPtr shall either point to a lin ear buffer of Availa bleLength bytes containing the data for transmission or be a NULL_PTR. For data transmission the service TcpIp_TcpTransmit() shall either use all data from the linear buffer if DataPtr is not a NULL_PTR , or retrieve up to AvailableL engt h data bytes from th e upper layer by calling Up _CopyTxData() one or multiple times in the context of this service otherwise ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00125",
   "text": "The service TcpIp_TcpTransmit() shall retrieve exactly AvailableLength bytes from the upper layer if the parameter DataPtr is a NULL_PTR and ForceRetrieve is TRUE. (If DataPtr is a NULL_PTR and ForceRetrieve is FALSE, TcpIp may ret rieve less data then available)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00126",
   "text": "Name Tcp Ip_ Param Id Type Kind Type Derived from uint8 Range TCPIP_ PARAMID_ TCP_ RXWND_ MAX 0x00 Specifies the maximum TCP receive window for the socket. [uint16] TCPIP_ PARAMID_ FRAMEPRIO 0x01 Specifies the frame priority for outgoing frames on the socket. [uint8] TCPIP_ PARAMID_ TCP_ NAGLE 0x02 Specifies if the Nagle Algorithm according to IETF RFC 1122 (chapter 4.2.3.4 When to Send Data) is enabled or not. [boolean] TCPIP_ PARAMID_ TCP_ KEEPALIVE 0x03 Specifies if TCP Keep Alive Probes are sent on the socket connection. [boolean] TCPIP_ PARAMID_ TTL 0x04 Specifies the time to live value…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00127",
   "text": "In case multiple IP address assignment methods are configured and a new address from an assignment method with a higher priority (1 is highest) becomes available, TcpIp shall use the new IP address and release the IP address previou sly assigned by an assignmen t method with a lower priority."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00128",
   "text": "If d evelopment error detection is enabled, the service TcpIp_ <Up> GetSocket() shall check the parameter Domain for being valid and raise the development error TCPIP_E_AFNOSUPPORT if it is invalid."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00130",
   "text": "T he Local IP address used for a socket is specified via TcpIp_Bind()."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00131",
   "text": "TcpIp shall always call EthIf_Transmit () with parameter TxConfirmation set to FALSE ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00132",
   "text": "Name Tcp Ip Ip6Addr Wildcard Type Kind Type Derived from uint32 Range TCPIP_ IP6ADDR_ ANY implementation specific defines the value used as wildcard for all IP6 address parts Description IP6 address wildcard. Available via Tcp Ip.h"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00133",
   "text": "Name Tcp Ip Ip Addr Wildcard Type Kind Type Derived from uint32 Range TCPIP_ IPADDR_ ANY implementation specific defines the value used as wildcard Description IP address wildcard. Available via Tcp Ip.h"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00134",
   "text": "Name Tcp Ip Port Wildcard Type Kind Type Derived from uint16 Range TCPIP_ PORT_ ANY -- Zero (0) is used as wildcard Description Port wildcard. Available via Tcp Ip.h Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 61 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00135",
   "text": "Name Tcp Ip Local Addr Id Wildcard Type Kind Type Derived from Tcp Ip _ Local Addr Id Type Range TCPIP_ LOCALADDRID_ ANY implementation specific defines the value used as wildcard Description Local Addr Id wildcard. Available via Tcp Ip.h"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00136",
   "text": "The TcpIp module shall initiate according actions to achieve the requested state if the stored state request is not the active state."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00137",
   "text": "Service Name Tcp Ip_ Get Remote Phys Addr Syntax Tcp Ip_ Return Type Tcp Ip_ Get Remote Phys Addr ( uint8 Ctrl Idx, const Tcp Ip_ Sock Addr Type* Ip Addr Ptr, uint8* Phys Addr Ptr, boolean init Res ) Service ID [hex] 0x16 Sync/ Async Synchronous Reentrancy Non Reentrant Parameters (in) Ctrl Idx Eth If controller index to identify the related ARP/ NDP table . Ip Addr Ptr specifies the IP address for which the physical address shall be retrieved init Res specifies if the address resolution shall be initiated (TRUE) or not (FALSE) in case the physical address related to the specified IP address…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00138",
   "text": "TcpIp_GetRemotePhysAddr shall lookup the physical address for the IP address specified by IpAddrPtr at the IP/physical address translatio n table related to the controller identified by CtrlIdx. (1) If the physical address is already known, PhysAddrPtr shall be set to the related physical address and the function shall return with TCPIP_E_OK. Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 86 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp (2) Otherwise it shall (a) initiate an address re solution if parameter initRes is set to TRUE and (b) return with TCPIP_E_PHYS_ADDR_MISS . PhysAddrPtr is no…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00139",
   "text": "TcpIp_GetRemotePhysAddr shall immediately return with TCPIP_E_NOT_OK if it is called with an IP address that is not part of the same sub network as the local address currently assigned to the controller identified by CtrlIdx."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00140",
   "text": "Service Name Tcp Ip_ Get Ctrl Idx Syntax Std_ Return Type Tcp Ip_ Get Ctrl Idx ( Tcp Ip_ Local Addr Id Type Local Addr Id, uint8* Ctrl Idx Ptr ) Service ID [hex] 0x17 Sync/ Async Synchronous Reentrancy Reentrant Parameters (in) Local Addr Id Local address identifier implicitely specif ing the Eth If controller that shall be returned. Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) Ctrl Idx Ptr Pointer to the memory where the index of the controller related to Local Addr Id is stored Return value Std _ Return - Type Result of operation E_ OK the request was successful E_ NOT_ OK the request was not s…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00141",
   "text": "TcpIp_GetCtrlIdx shall return the index of the controller related t o LocalAddrId."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00142",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall call <Up_PhysAddrTableChg > () directly after each ARP table change: (a) If TcpIp ad ds a new entry or updates an existing one, the parameter valid shall be set to TRUE and the paramet ers IpAddrPtr and PhysAddrPtr shall be set according to the new or updated entry. (b) In case TcpIp removes an entry, valid shall be set to FALSE and the parameters IpAddrPtr and PhysAddrPtr shall be set according to the removed entry."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00143",
   "text": "Service Name <Up_ Phys Addr Table Chg> Syntax void <Up_ Phys Addr Table Chg> ( uint8 Ctrl Idx, const Tcp Ip_ Sock Addr Type* Ip Addr Ptr, const uint8* Phys Addr Ptr, boolean valid ) Sync/ Async Synchronous Reentrancy Non Reentrant Parameters (in) Ctrl Idx Eth If controller index of the related ARP/ NDP table. Ip Addr Ptr specifies the IP address of the changed ARP/ NDP table entry Phys Addr Ptr specifies the physical address of the changed ARP/ NDP table entry valid specifies if the ARP/ NDP table entry is added or changed (TRUE) or has been removed (FALSE) Parameters None Specification of TC…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00144",
   "text": "The TcpIp module shall indicate events related to sockets to the upper layer module by using the Up _TcpIpEvent API and the follo wing events: TCPIP_TCP_RESET, TCPIP_TCP_CLOSED, TCPIP_TCP_FIN_RECEIVED and TCPIP_UDP_CLOSED ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00146",
   "text": "TcpIp_Bind () shall check if there is another socket already bound to the same port, protocol and local address and if that is the case refuse the request and return E_NOT_OK. If development error detection is enabled, the service TcpIp_Bind () shall also raise the development error code TCPIP_E_ADDRINUSE."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00147",
   "text": "If development error detection is enabled: TcpIp_Bind() shall check if the parameter LocalAddrId is valid. If the check fails, TcpIp_Bind() shall refuse the request and raise the development error code TCPIP_E_ADDRNOTAVAIL instead ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00150",
   "text": "The TcpIp module for IPv4 an d IPv6 (Dual Stack) – In - Vehicle and Diagnosti c Communication (S calability class 3) shall support th e feat ures listed in Figure 3 : TcpIp Scalability Classes , column Scalability Class 3."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00152",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the Ful ly Qualified Domain Name Option for Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv4 Client requirements as defined in IETF RFC 4702 (The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv4 (DHCPv4) Client Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) Option). No DNS shall be s upported. Only section 2 The Client FQDN Option and section 3 DHCP Client Behavior shall be supported. Sub - Section 3.2, 3.3, 3.5 shall not be supported."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00153",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the frame format for transmission of IPv6 packets and the method of forming IPv6 link - local addresses and statelessly autoconfigured addresses on Ethernet networks as defined in IETF RFC 2464 (Transmission of IPv6 Packets over Ethernet Networks)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00154",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the source address selection algorithm as defined in IETF RFC 6724 (Default Address Selection for Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6)). Only section 5 Source Address Selection shall be supported."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00155",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the section 4 , first paragraph of the IETF RFC 5722 (Handling of Overlapping IPv6 Fragments). The IETF RFC 5722 demonstrates the security issues associated with allowing overlapping fragments and u pdates the IPv6 specification to explicitly forbid overlapping fragments (transmission and reception) ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00157",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the section 5.1. Node Configuration Variables, section 5.3. C reation of Link - Local Addresses, section 5.4, Duplicate Address Detection, section 5.5 Creation of Global Addresses and section 5.6 Configuration Consistency of the IETF RFC 4862 (IPv6 Stateless Address Autoconfiguration)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00159",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the Duplicate Address Detection as defined in IETF RFC 4429 (Optimistic Duplicate Address Detection (DAD) for IPv6)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00160",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the basic IPv6 header and the initially defined IPv6 e xtension headers and options as defined in IETF RFC 8200 (Internet Protocol, Version 6 (IPv6) Specification) ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00161",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the reception and reassembly of fragmented IPv6 frames according to IETF RFC 8200 Section 4.5 Fragm ent Header ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00163",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the Internet Control Message Protocol Version 6 as defined in IETF RFC 4443 (Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMPv6) for the Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) Specification)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00164",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the Neighb or Discovery protocol for IP Version 6 as defined in IETF RFC 4861 (Neighbor Discovery for IP version 6 (IPv6)) except the sections 4.5 Redirect Message Format, 6.2. Router Specification, 7.2.8. Proxy Neighbor Advertisements and 8. Redirect Function ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00166",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the client part of the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv6 (DHCPv6) which enables DHCP servers to pass configuration parameters such as IPv6 network addre sses to IPv6 nodes as defined in IETF RFC 3315 (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv6 (DHCPv6)). Due to the fact that only the client functionality shall be supported, the following sections shall not be supported: • Relay Agent Behavior • Server Beh avior • Section 12. Management of Temporary Addresses • Section 21. Authentication of DHCP Messages • Section 22.5. Identity Association for Temporary Ad…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00167",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the Fully Qualified Domain Name Option for Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv6 Client requirements as defined in IETF RFC 4704 (The Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol for IPv6 (DHCPv6) Client Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) Option). No DNS shall be supported. Only section 4 DHCPv6 Client FQDN Option and section 5 DHCPv6 Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 41 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp Client Behavior shall be supported. Sub - Section 5.1, 5.2, 5.4 shall not be supported."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00168",
   "text": "The TcpIp shall support the specific algorithm for responding to partial acknowledgments as defined in IETF RFC 6582 (The NewReno Modification to TCP's Fast Rec overy Algorithm).The modification shall only be used if the Fast Recovery strategy of IETF RFC 5681 is enabled."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00169",
   "text": "T he TcpIp IP - layer shall map received IP datagrams to an entry in the local address table (TcpIpAddrId). The local address table mapping is successfully if ALL of the following conditions are fulfilled: a) The receiving interface matches the interface assigned to the local address table entry (EthIfCtrl). b) T he destination IP address contained in the IP header matches the currently assigned IP address of the local address table entry. All IP datagrams which cannot be mapped to an entry in the local address table shall be silently discarded. All successfully mapped IP datagrams shall be f…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00170",
   "text": "The TcpIp UDP - layer shall map received UDP datagrams to sockets based on the destination port as contained in the UDP protocol header and the local ad d ress (TcpIpAddrId). The local address (TcpIpAddrId) matches if ANY o f the following conditions is fulfilled: Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 42 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp a) The socket is bound to the local address (TcpIpAddrId) b) The socket local address uses the wildcard “ANY” AND the socket EthIfCtrl is identical to the EthIfCtrl used in the local address (TcpIpAddrId) c) The socket is bo und to TCPIP…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00171",
   "text": "For received UDP datagrams where the local address (TcpIpAddrId) is a broadcast or multicast address, all matching sockets shall receive the incoming message."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00172",
   "text": "The TcpIp TCP - layer shall map received TCP datagrams to sockets based on the destination port as contained in t he TCP protocol header and the local address (TcpIpAddrId). The local address (TcpIpAddrId) matches if ANY of the following conditions is fu l filled: a) The socket is bound to a unicast local address (TcpIpAddrId) b) The socket local address uses the wildcard “AN Y” AND the socket EthIfCtrl is identical to the EthIfCtrl used in the local address (TcpIpAddrId) c) The socket is bound to TCPIP_LOCALADDRID_ANY"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00173",
   "text": "Sockets with established TCP connections shall match source port, source IP address, destination port and destination IP address as contained in the protocol headers additionally to the generic TCP mapping criteria described in [SWS_TCPIP_00172] ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00174",
   "text": "Received TCP datagrams where the local address (TcpIpAddrId) is a broadcast or multicast addres s, shall be silently discarded."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00175",
   "text": "If data is transmitted using a socket which is bound to an IPv4 Unicast local address (TcpIpAddrId) the TcpIp shall use the IP address assigned to the local address (TcpIpAddrId) as source IP address in the IP datagram header. The IP datagram shall be transmitted using the EthIfCtrl the local address (TcpIpAddrId) is m apped to."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00176",
   "text": "If data is transmitted using an IPv4 socket which is bound to a local address (TcpIpAddrId) using the wildcard “ANY”, then the TcpIp shall use the IP address of the configured local address (TcpIpAddrId), which is of type IPv4 Unica st and assigned to the same EthIfCtrl, as the bound local address (TcpIpAddrId) as source IP address in the IP datagram header."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00177",
   "text": "If data is transmitted using an IPv4 socket which is bound to TCPIP_LOCALADDRID_ANY, then the TcpIp shall use the IP address of the configured local address (TcpIpAddrId), which is of type IPv4 Unicast and assigned to the EthIfCtrl in the same subnet as the destination IPv4 address as source IP address in the IP datagram header. If no matching subnet is found the IPv4 Unicast local address (TcpIpAddrId) of EthIfCtrl = 0 is selected."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00178",
   "text": "If data is transmitted using an IPv4 UDP socket which is bound to a local address (TcpIpAddrId) of type Multicast, then the TcpIp shall use the IP address of the configured local address (TcpIpAddrId), which is of type IPv4 Unicast and assigned to the same EthIfCtrl, as the bound local address (TcpIpAddrId) as source IP address in the IP datagram header."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00179",
   "text": "If data is transmitted using an IPv4 UDP socket which is bound to a local address (TcpIpAddrId) of type Broa dcast, then the TcpIp shall use the IP address of the configured local address (TcpIpAddrId), which is of type IPv4 Unicast and assigned to the same EthIfCtrl, as the bound local address (TcpIpAddrId) as source IP address in the IP datagram header."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00181",
   "text": "If data is transmitted using a socket which is bound to an IPv6 Unicast local address (TcpIpAddrId) the TcpIp shall use the IP address assigned to local address (TcpIpAddrId) as source IP address in the IP datagram header. The IP Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 45 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp datagram shall be transmitted using the EthIfCtrl the local address (TcpIpAddrId) is mapped to."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00182",
   "text": "If data is transmitted using an IPv6 socket which is bound to a local address (TcpIpAddrId) using the wildcard “ANY”, the TcpIp shall select the source IP address of the IPv6 header according to the source address selection algorith m spe cified in section 5 of IETF RFC 6724 (Default Address Selection for IPv6). The selection shall be limited to the configured local addresses (TcpIpAddrId) on the same EthIfCtrl as the bound local address (TcpIpAddrId) only."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00183",
   "text": "If da ta is transmitted using an IPv6 socket which is bound to TCPIP_LOCALADDRID_ANY, the TcpIp shall select the interface that has a local address (TcpIpAddrId) which uses the same network prefix as the destination address. If no matching interface is found Eth IfCtrl = 0 is selected. The TcpIp shall select the source IP address of the IPv6 header according to the source address selection algorithm spe cified in section 5 of IETF RFC 6724 (Default Address Selection for IPv6)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00184",
   "text": "If data is transmitted using an IPv6 UDP socket which is bound to a local address (TcpIpAddrId) of type Multicast, the TcpIp - shall select the source IP address of the IPv6 header according to the source address selection algorithm sp ecified in section 5 of IETF RFC 6724 (Default Address Selection for IPv6). The selection shall be limited to the configured local addresses (TcpIpAddrId) on the same EthIfCtrl as the bound local address (TcpIpAddrId) only."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00185",
   "text": "If dat a is transmitted using an IPv6 UDP socket which is not bound, the TcpIp shall select the interface that has a local address (TcpIpAddrId) which uses the same network prefix as the destination address. If no matching interface is found EthIfCtrl = 0 is sele cted. The TcpIp shall select the source IP address of the IPv6 header according to the source address selection algorithm specifi ed in section 5 of IETF RFC 6724 (Default Address Selection for IPv6)."
  },

   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00191",
   "text": "If the parameter TcpIpArpPacketQueueEnabled is set to TRUE and an IPv4 packet shall be transmitted to a remote host but the related link layer address does not exist i n the ARP table, the TcpIp shall start the address Specification of TCP/IP Stack AUTO SAR CP R20 - 11 46 of 293 Document ID 617 : AUTOSAR_SWS_TcpIp resolution and queue this packet according to IETF RFC 1122, section 2.3.2.2 and accept the transmission request with E_OK ."

  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00192",
   "text": "If the parameter TcpIpArpPacketQueueEnabled is set to FALS E and an IPv4 packet shall be transmitted to a remote host but the related link layer address does not exist in the ARP table, the TcpIp shall start the address resolution but reject the transmission request with E_NOT_OK."

  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_TCPIP_00195",

  },

   "text": "If the configuration contains TcpIpDhcpAddressAssignments that refer to specific ports of an Ethernet Switch, DHCP server shall identify the port the request was received from , by calling EthIf_GetPortMacAddr() with the M AC address of the DHCP client and choose an available IP address of the TcpIpDhcpAddressAssignment related to the same port."
